nipo.vintage_label: Global Trade Alert, New Industrial Policy Observatory, June 2026 extract (synthetic)
nipo.staged_d: Global Trade Alert's measures are not yet matched to the six supply-chain stages, so they are counted for the whole economy and not listed by sector.
nipo.strength_words: Strength scores a measure by the bite of its instrument (a grant, loan, local-content rule or import ban counts more than monitoring), whether Global Trade Alert judges it to favour domestic firms, how widely it applies (a whole sector counts more than one named firm) and the money or trade it covers; measures that are part of a package of several instrument types count up to 60% more.
nipo.confidence_words: Mapping confidence says how firmly the measure's product list and text tie it to energy sectors (averaged over the sectors it maps to): 0.10 when none of its listed products are energy-sector goods, 0.25 for a measure without a product list, from 0.75 up when its products fall in these sectors, and up to 2 when its title, source and Global Trade Alert's sector flags corroborate the mapping.

caveats.text: Scores compare Puerto Rico with other economies in the same sector; they are not measures of risk or profit in absolute terms.
All index values are the NEIS baseline as of 12 October 2026, scored at six supply-chain stages; Strategic Insights recomputes them under other weightings.
Some of Puerto Rico's sectors are not placed: a score is compared with other economies only when the economy is sovereign and at most half of the score rests on filled-in data.

The Climate Action Tracker does not rate Puerto Rico, so its policy activity rests on International Energy Agency Policies and Measures records alone; its policy levels compare only with economies on the same basis.
Puerto Rico has no Strategic Index because it has no International Energy Agency Policies and Measures records.
Puerto Rico has no UN votes of its own; its alignment is the United States'.

Factory projects are cross-border solar, wind, battery and electric-vehicle manufacturing projects only, announced projects included, which may never be built; domestic investment is not covered (Cleantech Manufacturing FDI Dataset, edition 2026.10.05, CC BY 4.0; counts by the authors, a joint venture counted under its listed parent). The data do not say which part of manufacturing a project serves, so Components and Assembly show the same projects; totals count each project once.
Where Puerto Rico or a partner did not report a flow, it is read from the other side's report, raised by 6% to value it like imports.
Hong Kong's trade is largely re-exports.
A parent's home is where it is headquartered, not its ultimate owner.
